stories.headline: S&P 500 HITS RECORD 7,600 TO START JUNE; NASDAQ TOPS 27,000 FOR FIRST TIME
stories.body: Stocks opened June with records across the board: S&P 500 +0.26% to 7,600, Nasdaq +0.42% to 27,087 — first-ever close above 27K. Tech and energy led the gains despite a 5.7% oil surge; the index is now on a 10-consecutive-week winning streak, its longest since 2017.

stories.headline: IRAN HALTS US CEASEFIRE TALKS; WTI SURGES 5.7% TO $92
stories.body: Iran suspended ceasefire negotiations with the US on Monday, sending WTI crude up 5.7% to $92 and reversing part of May's 17% oil decline. Gold fell 2.7% to $4,455 as the dollar (DXY +0.4% to 99.3) absorbed safe-haven flows; yields eased slightly to 4.44% (-1 bps) despite the flare-up.

stories.headline: SPURS DOWN THUNDER IN GAME 7; WEMBY HEADS TO NBA FINALS VS. KNICKS
stories.body: Victor Wembanyama (22 pts, 7 reb) guided San Antonio past Oklahoma City 111-103 in a Game 7 thriller Saturday. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander had 35 for OKC in a losing effort. NBA Finals: Spurs vs. Knicks tips off Wednesday June 3 at 8:30 PM ET on ABC in San Antonio — Spurs have home court (62-20 regular season).

stories.headline: EAGLES TRADE A.J. BROWN TO PATRIOTS FOR 2028 FIRST-ROUND PICK
stories.body: Philadelphia sent star receiver A.J. Brown to New England for a 2028 first-round pick and 2027 fifth-rounder, timing the deal after June 1 to split $43.5M in dead cap across two seasons ($16.3M in '26, $27.1M in '27). Brown, 28, becomes the Patriots' WR1 immediately.

stories.headline: UW OPENS 2026 SEASON VS. WASHINGTON STATE ON NBC; BIG TEN TICKETS JUNE 15
stories.body: Washington released its first three game times for 2026: Boeing Apple Cup vs. Washington State on Sunday Sept. 6 at 1 PM PT on NBC, followed by Utah State (Sept. 12) and Eastern Washington (Sept. 19) on Big Ten Network. Single-game Big Ten home tickets go on sale to the public June 15.

stories.headline: TRANSFER PORTAL WINDS DOWN AS BLUE BLOODS RELOAD; NCAA CONFIRMS 76-TEAM FIELD
stories.body: As the portal window closes, Kentucky added Washington's Zoom Diallo to its offseason haul while Danny Sprinkle brought in Ryan Beasley (USF, 13.6 ppg, All-WCC) and Gonzaga grad Steele Venters to rebuild the Huskies. The NCAA confirmed the men's tournament will expand to 76 teams in a future cycle.

deepDive.title: Iran Flares, Oil Spikes — But Stocks Hit a Record Anyway. The Decoupling Explained.
content: WTI crude surged 5.7% to $92 on Monday after Iran halted US ceasefire talks, delivering the kind of geopolitical shock that three years ago would have sent the S&P into the red. Instead, stocks closed at an all-time high of 7,600. The headline captured the dynamic precisely: 'tech rally overpowers oil spike.' Understanding how this is possible — and when it stops being possible — is one of the most useful macro questions to internalize right now.

The key is recognizing that oil's relationship to equities depends critically on which driver is causing it to move. Demand-pull oil (rising because the global economy is strong) tends to be equity-neutral or mildly positive. Supply-shock oil (rising because of a geopolitical disruption, OPEC cut, or blockage) functions as a tax on consumer and corporate cash flows and historically compresses P/E multiples. Today's Iran spike is clearly the second type — a risk-premium re-injection into crude futures, not a signal of surging demand. The market is betting the shock is temporary. Tech valuations, which rest on discounted future cash flows, are far more sensitive to interest rate expectations than to short-term commodity prices — and with the 10-year yield easing to 4.44%, the rate math still supports elevated multiples.

Compare to March 2022: Russia invaded Ukraine, WTI surged from $75 to $130, and the S&P fell roughly 15% over the following weeks. The critical difference was the macro backdrop, not merely the magnitude of the oil move. In early 2022, headline CPI was at 7.9% and accelerating, the Fed had not yet hiked once, and Treasury yields were repricing sharply as the Fed was forced to react aggressively. That combination — a commodity spike into already-hot inflation, forcing an accelerating hiking cycle — crushed equity multiples. Today CPI is near 2.5%, the Fed is near neutral, and the AI buildout narrative provides tech stocks a compelling long-run productivity story. Oil at $92 for a single trading session does not change the 3-month forward inflation picture meaningfully.

Where this decoupling breaks down is if WTI holds above $90 for six to eight weeks — long enough to pass through into energy services prices and appear in the June and July CPI prints. The June 5 Jobs Report is the first major data point: a strong print above +175K combined with persistently elevated oil would push the Fed back toward 'higher for longer' language, pressure long yields upward, and eventually compress the tech multiples currently holding the record-setting market aloft. For now the oil spike is a one-day story. If Iran's breakdown proves durable, it becomes a macro regime question — and the rate-cut bets priced into markets for late 2026 would face serious pressure.
